works/darby-hopes-of-the-church/title: The Hopes of the Church of God in Connexion with the Destiny of the Jews and the Nations
works/darby-hopes-of-the-church/summary: Lectures delivered by Darby in Geneva in 1840 setting out a distinction between God’s heavenly people (the Church) and earthly people (Israel).
works/darby-hopes-of-the-church/signific: An early systematic statement of the Israel–Church distinction and the Church’s heavenly hope that underlie dispensationalism.
works/scofield-reference-bible/summary: King James Bible with Cyrus Scofield’s headings, cross-references and notes, published by Oxford University Press (revised 1917).
works/scofield-reference-bible/significa: Carried dispensational premillennialism into millions of homes and Bible institutes; arguably the most influential single vehicle of the doctrine.
works/dodd-parables-of-the-kingdom/summa: Dodd’s study arguing that Jesus’ parables announce the kingdom as already present in his ministry.
works/ladd-presence-of-the-future/summar: Revised edition of Ladd’s Jesus and the Kingdom (1964), arguing that the kingdom is God’s dynamic reign, inaugurated in Jesus and consummated at his return.
works/ladd-presence-of-the-future/signif: Brought inaugurated ("already/not yet") eschatology into the evangelical mainstream.
works/muntzer-sermon-to-the-princes/summ: Thomas Müntzer’s exposition of Daniel 2 preached before Duke John of Saxony at Allstedt, 13 July 1524.
works/muntzer-sermon-to-the-princes/sign: Urged the princes to wield the sword against the godless in the last days; a key text of revolutionary apocalypticism before the Peasants’ War.
works/tertullian-on-idolatry/summary: Tertullian’s rigorist guide to avoiding complicity with idolatry in trades, festivals, offices and military service.
works/tertullian-on-idolatry/significanc: Classic early argument that Christians may not serve as soldiers.
works/origen-against-celsus/summary: Eight-book reply to the pagan philosopher Celsus’ True Word.
works/origen-against-celsus/significance: Book 8.73–75 defends Christians’ refusal of military service: they serve the emperor by prayer.
works/eusebius-life-of-constantine/summa: Eusebius’ panegyrical biography of Constantine, completed after the emperor’s death (337).
works/eusebius-life-of-constantine/signi: Source of the vision of the cross ("Conquer by this") and of the Christian imperial ideology of the Byzantine world.
works/augustine-against-faustus/title: Reply to Faustus the Manichaean (Contra Faustum)
works/augustine-against-faustus/summary: Thirty-three books answering the Manichaean bishop Faustus’ attacks on the Old Testament.
works/augustine-against-faustus/signific: Book 22.74–79 contains Augustine’s key reflections on the morality of war.
works/gelasius-famuli-vestrae/title: Letter to Emperor Anastasius (Famuli vestrae pietatis)
works/gelasius-famuli-vestrae/summary: Gelasius I’s letter distinguishing priestly authority from royal power.
works/gelasius-famuli-vestrae/significan: Foundational text of the medieval "two swords" tradition.
works/aquinas-summa-theologiae/significa: II-II q.40 sets out the classic conditions of a just war; III q.73–83 treats the Eucharist and transubstantiation.
works/luther-temporal-authority/title: Temporal Authority: To What Extent It Should Be Obeyed
works/luther-temporal-authority/summary: Luther’s treatise distinguishing God’s two governments, spiritual and temporal.
works/luther-temporal-authority/signific: Classic statement of the Lutheran two-kingdoms teaching.
works/schleitheim-confession/summary: Seven articles agreed by Swiss Brethren at Schleitheim under Michael Sattler: baptism, the ban, the breaking of bread, separation, pastors, the sword and the oath.
works/schleitheim-confession/significanc: Defining statement of separatist, nonresistant Anabaptism.
works/quaker-peace-testimony/title: A Declaration from the Harmless and Innocent People of God, called Quakers
works/quaker-peace-testimony/summary: Declaration presented to Charles II by George Fox and others after the Fifth Monarchist rising.
works/quaker-peace-testimony/significanc: Founding statement of the Quaker Peace Testimony.
works/douglass-narrative/title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
works/douglass-narrative/summary: Douglass’ autobiography of his life in slavery and escape.
works/douglass-narrative/significance: Its appendix distinguishes "the Christianity of Christ" from slaveholding religion.
works/stringfellow-brief-examination/tit: A Brief Examination of Scripture Testimony on the Institution of Slavery
works/stringfellow-brief-examination/sum: Pro-slavery biblical tract arguing that slavery was sanctioned in the patriarchal age, by the Mosaic law and by Christ and the apostles.
works/stringfellow-brief-examination/sig: Widely circulated example of antebellum pro-slavery exegesis, now universally repudiated.
works/rauschenbusch-christianity-social-: Rauschenbusch’s history of the prophets, Jesus and the Church as a social movement, with a call to reform industrial capitalism.
Bestselling manifesto of the Social Gospel.
works/rauschenbusch-theology-social-gosp: A Theology for the Social Gospel
Rauschenbusch’s systematic theology built around the kingdom of God and "super-personal forces of evil".
Theological summa of the Social Gospel, later admired by Martin Luther King Jr.
works/barmen-declaration/summary: Six theses adopted by the Confessing Church synod at Barmen (29–31 May 1934), largely drafted by Karl Barth.
works/barmen-declaration/significance: Rejected the subordination of the Church to the Nazi state and the "German Christians"; a model for later confessions of resistance (e.g. Belhar 1986).
works/gutierrez-theology-of-liberation/t: A Theology of Liberation (Teología de la liberación: Perspectivas)
works/gutierrez-theology-of-liberation/s: Gutiérrez’s foundational work defining theology as critical reflection on Christian praxis in the light of the Word, from the standpoint of the poor.
Founding text of Latin American liberation theology.
works/king-letter-birmingham-jail/summar: King’s open letter (16 April 1963) answering white clergy who called his campaign "unwise and untimely".
works/king-letter-birmingham-jail/signif: Classic Christian defence of nonviolent civil disobedience against unjust laws.
works/tertullian-against-praxeas/summary: Tertullian’s refutation of the modalist Praxeas, written after he had embraced the New Prophecy.
works/tertullian-against-praxeas/signifi: First Latin use of "trinitas" in a developed sense; also a Montanist-era polemic accusing Praxeas of driving out the Paraclete.
works/basil-on-the-holy-spirit/title: On the Holy Spirit (De Spiritu Sancto)
works/basil-on-the-holy-spirit/summary: Basil’s defence of the full divinity of the Spirit and of the doxology "with the Spirit", against the Pneumatomachi.
works/basil-on-the-holy-spirit/significa: Prepared the way for the confession of the Spirit as "Lord and Giver of Life" at Constantinople (381); key source for unwritten apostolic tradition.
works/chrysostom-homilies-1-corinthians/: Forty-four homilies preached at Antioch on 1 Corinthians.
Homily 29 on 1 Corinthians 12 records that the charismata described by Paul no longer occurred in Chrysostom’s day, a text later cited by cessationists.
works/augustine-homilies-1-john/title: Homilies (Tractates) on the First Epistle of John
works/augustine-homilies-1-john/summary: Ten Easter-season sermons on love in 1 John.
works/augustine-homilies-1-john/signific: Contains the classic "signs adapted to the time" passage on tongues (6.10) and the saying "love, and do what you will" (7.8).
works/warfield-counterfeit-miracles/summ: Warfield’s Thomas Smyth lectures (Columbia Seminary, 1917) surveying patristic, medieval, Irvingite, faith-healing and Christian Science miracle claims.
works/warfield-counterfeit-miracles/sign: The classic statement of modern Protestant cessationism.
works/wesley-more-excellent-way/summary: Wesley’s sermon on 1 Corinthians 12:31 contrasting extraordinary gifts with the "more excellent way" of love.
works/wesley-more-excellent-way/signific: Argues the extraordinary gifts declined because love grew cold after Constantine, not because God withdrew them: an early non-cessationist reading influential on Holiness and Pentecostal movements.
works/apostolic-faith-newspaper/summary: Newspaper published from the Azusa Street Mission, edited by William J. Seymour and Clara Lum (1906–08), reaching tens of thousands of readers worldwide.
works/apostolic-faith-newspaper/signific: Spread news of the Azusa Street revival and Pentecostal doctrine globally.
works/wimber-power-evangelism/summary: John Wimber (with Kevin Springer) on evangelism accompanied by healing, deliverance and words of knowledge as signs of the kingdom.
works/wimber-power-evangelism/significan: Manifesto of the "Third Wave", drawing on George Ladd’s kingdom theology.
works/wagner-churchquake/title: Churchquake! How the New Apostolic Reformation Is Shaking Up the Church As We Know It
works/wagner-churchquake/summary: C. Peter Wagner’s account of networks led by contemporary apostles and prophets.
works/wagner-churchquake/significance: Named and promoted the New Apostolic Reformation.
works/tertullian-on-the-soul/summary: The first Christian treatise on psychology: the soul is corporeal in a subtle sense, originates with the body and is transmitted from parents (traducianism).
works/tertullian-on-the-soul/significanc: Classic source of traducianism and of the Western link between generation and inherited sin.
works/tertullian-apparel-of-women/title: On the Apparel of Women (De cultu feminarum)
works/tertullian-apparel-of-women/summar: Ascetic exhortation to Christian women to modesty, opening with an address to every woman as an Eve.
works/tertullian-apparel-of-women/signif: Frequently cited in histories of Christian misogyny and of gendered readings of the fall.
works/gregory-nyssa-making-of-man/title: On the Making of Man (De hominis opificio)
works/gregory-nyssa-making-of-man/summar: Completes Basil’s Hexaemeron with a treatise on humanity: the image of God in human freedom and reason, humanity as a whole (pleroma) created in the image, and the body-soul relation.
works/chrysostom-homilies-romans/summary: Thirty-two homilies preached at Antioch on Paul’s letter to the Romans.
works/chrysostom-homilies-romans/signifi: Represents the Antiochene and later Eastern reading of Romans 5: Adam’s descendants inherit mortality and liability, not personal guilt.
works/erasmus-free-will/title: On Free Will (De libero arbitrio diatribe)
works/erasmus-free-will/summary: Argues from Scripture and the Fathers that the human will, aided by grace, has a real if small power to apply itself to salvation.
works/erasmus-free-will/significance: Provoked Luther’s The Bondage of the Will (1525).
works/zwingli-original-sin/title: Declaration on Original Sin (De peccato originali declaratio)
works/zwingli-original-sin/summary: Addressed to Urbanus Rhegius, it describes original sin as an inherited disease or defect (morbus) rather than personal guilt, and doubts the damnation of children of believers dying in infancy.
works/zwingli-original-sin/significance: The main Reformation-era alternative to the inherited-guilt doctrine.
works/edwards-freedom-of-the-will/title: A Careful and Strict Enquiry into … Freedom of Will
works/edwards-freedom-of-the-will/summar: Argues that the will is always determined by the strongest motive, so that moral necessity is compatible with freedom and responsibility, against Arminian notions of self-determination.
works/edwards-original-sin/title: The Great Christian Doctrine of Original Sin Defended
works/edwards-original-sin/summary: Defends original sin against John Taylor of Norwich, arguing that God constitutes Adam and his posterity as one, as he constitutes the identity of any thing through time.
works/edwards-original-sin/significance: Influential realist-federal account of humanity’s solidarity in Adam.
works/nee-spiritual-man/summary: Three volumes setting out a tripartite anthropology of spirit, soul and body and calling believers to live by the spirit rather than the soul.
works/nee-spiritual-man/significance: Spread trichotomist teaching through Chinese house churches and global evangelical and charismatic circles.
works/romanides-ancestral-sin/summary: Contrasts the Greek patristic understanding of Adam’s legacy (death and corruption) with Augustinian inherited guilt.
works/romanides-ancestral-sin/significan: Shaped a generation of Orthodox self-understanding over against the West.
works/protoevangelium-of-james/summary: An apocryphal infancy narrative telling of Mary's miraculous birth to Joachim and Anne, her upbringing in the Temple, her betrothal to the elderly widower Joseph, and the virgin birth.
works/protoevangelium-of-james/significa: Shaped Marian feasts (Nativity and Presentation of Mary), art and the Eastern view of Jesus' ‘brothers’ as Joseph's sons; never canonical.
works/jerome-against-helvidius/title: The Perpetual Virginity of Blessed Mary (Against Helvidius)
works/jerome-against-helvidius/summary: Jerome's polemic arguing that Jesus' ‘brothers’ were cousins and that Mary remained a virgin.
works/jerome-against-helvidius/significa: The classic Western defence of Mary's perpetual virginity.
works/john-damascus-on-holy-images/title: Apologies against Those Who Attack the Divine Images
works/john-damascus-on-holy-images/summa: Three treatises defending icons: the incarnation makes God depictable; veneration differs from worship; the testimony of the Fathers.
works/john-damascus-on-holy-images/signi: The foundational theology of icons, vindicated at Nicaea II.
works/second-nicaea-definition/title: Definition of the Second Council of Nicaea
works/second-nicaea-definition/summary: Decrees that images of Christ, Mary, angels and saints be set up and given honourable veneration (timetike proskynesis), not true worship (latreia), which belongs to the divine nature alone.
works/second-nicaea-definition/significa: The seventh ecumenical council recognised by Orthodox and Catholics.
